newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN raps both Croatia and Serbs in eastern Slavonia.
newsitem.headline: UN raps both Croatia and Serbs in eastern Slavonia.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council Friday backed April 13 as a date for holding local elections in the Croatian enclave of Eastern Slavonia, now under U.N. administration.

But at the same time the council, in a statement read at a formal meeting, criticised both Croatia and local Serbs in the region, which borders Yugoslavia's republic of Serbia, for throwing difficulties in the way of a smooth transition to Croatian rule.

Eastern Slavonia, which seceded from Croatia in 1991, opposing Zagreb's drive for independence from federal Yugoslavia, is monitored by about 5,000 U.N. peacekeepers as part of the U.N. Transitional Administration for Eastern Slavonia, known as UNTAES, headed by Jacques Klein, an American. Its mandate ends on July 15.

The Council deplored "disruptive activities" by radicals in the Serb community who created "an atmosphere of political agitation and uncertainty" discouraging people from taking out Croatian citizenship and encouraging them to leave the area.
"It calls upon all residents of the region to follow wise leadership, to stay in the region, and to take up their future as citizens oif the Republic of Croatia," the council said.

The Croatian government, the council said, had to issue documents quicker than it has as well as prepare properly for the elections. It also called on Croatia to apply its amnesty law fairly and consistently to Serbs in the region.

"The long-term success of peaceful reintegration will be determined by the commitment of the Government of Croatia to reconciliation and to ensuring that those Serbs who are currently resident in the region will enjoy equal rights as Croatian citizens," the council said.
The Council also critcized Croatia for making no progress on the future of displaced people and guaranteeing equal treatment to Serbs for housing and other social welfare grants.
The once-volatile region, dominated by Serbs and bordering the Yugoslav republic of Serbia, is the only remaining Croatian area not under Zagreb's control.
